items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Fernand never had a band of regular musicians although there were certain ones that usually gigged with him and I did a few with him.

ctx.x: The dancing schools were run by gangsters and the musicians were not supposed to look at the girls in a friendly manner. But the girls who really wanted to be with a musician would always find a way but it was the work and not the girls that I did not like in those places. Bobby Neal was the only dancing school leader that could work those places and make it more like working at the Savoy than any other leader of that type. I really had pleasure working with him. The musicians could relax by playing head numbers…

The Renaissance Ballroom at the corner of 138th Street and 7th Avenue was a place where most of the Negro clubs held their dances and the leader of the orchestra was a fellow named Fernand Andrade, a banjo and guitar player. Fernand never had a band of regular musicians although there were certain ones that usually gigged with him and I did a

few with him. There are many name musicians in the 20s and 30s that gigged at one time with Fernand; Benny Carter, Rex Stewart, Bobby Starke, etc. When I gigged with Fernand, I met one of the greatest alto sax men in the business. His name was Hilton Jefferson. Jeff was a very quiet man but he made his horn talk for him and all the musicians loved him.
